clue.text: Appear to assume everybody's lacking intellectual subtlety

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: to appear is to show up, so this gives SHOW
everybody is all, so this gives ALL

explanation.surface: Someone seems to take it for granted that everyone is a bit dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow thinking is superficial, lacking depth or intellectual subtlety.

clue.text: Begins cutting within seconds

indicators.note: within says the sharp word sits inside the seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, doubled for seconds
a cutting remark is tart, sharp

explanation.surface: Something gets under way by making cuts in mere seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to begin something is to start it.

clue.text: Tried to find a time to risk provoking newspaper boss

parts.note: to tempt fate is to risk provoking it
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone looked for a moment to goad the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Past-tense synonyms: having attempted something is having tried it.

clue.text: Delight in friend elevated into prominence

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word up the column reads it backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
things that come up come into prominence

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys seeing a friend raised to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up praise is to relish it eagerly, an idiom for delight in.

clue.text: Old team owner ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A former club owner has been brought to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture riddled by woodworm looks decrepit, so worm-eaten is used loosely for antiquated or old.

clue.text: Celeb overwhelmed by damaging allegations is hot stuff

indicators.note: being overwhelmed by something is being engulfed in it, so the celebrity sits inside

parts.note: slinging mud is making damaging allegations
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A celebrity buried by a scandal is still sizzling news.
explanation.definitionFit: The condiment is fiery on the tongue, literally hot stuff.

clue.text: Miles needs to remove source of pathogens from fruit tree

indicators.note: remove says a letter is taken away from the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone named Miles must clear a disease from an orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore's relative from which syrup comes is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Advantageously placed by drug producing plant

indicators.note: placed by means put next to, so the drug comes first and the adverb beside it

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
well is used for advantageously, as in well placed

explanation.surface: Something positioned well beside a drug yields a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, the small blue-flowered wildflower, is a plant of that name.

clue.text: Correct graduate over the last point

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns a word upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
the end is the last point

explanation.surface: A graduate is correct about the final point.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to correct a text is to revise or fix it.

clue.text: Be uncertain about turning up with it in the middle of Oldham

indicators.note: in places the small word inside those middle letters
the middle of the town name is its central pair of letters
turning up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure about appearing in central Oldham, a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the short word for concerning, flipped by 'turning up' since this is a down clue; the clue gives it first, but it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to waver indecisively, so it is to be uncertain.

clue.text: Malfunction leads to Bill getting deposit back

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to put something is to deposit it

explanation.surface: A fault results in a bill for returning a deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that acts up misbehaves, a phrasal verb for malfunctioning.

clue.text: State aim to stand by soldiers

indicators.note: standing by is standing next to, so the aiming word follows the soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to present a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A country intends to support its troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something as true is to state or assert it.

clue.text: Single article on period watch

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after, so the article follows the period

parts.note: a period is a time
a single article is a piece, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: One item's put on a period watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a portable clock, a type of instrument for keeping time.

clue.text: Party, for example, doing an about face over duke's dishonest act

parts.note: a do is a party
D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: doing an about face is turning round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A political party makes a U-turn over a nobleman's scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political but means a social do; 'doing an about face' turns only the example abbreviation, and 'over' simply puts it after the duke.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or scam, a dishonest act.

clue.text: Go crazy on the way back, for instance

indicators.note: on the way back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone loses it while returning home, say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is to have a stab, an attempt.

clue.text: Stay in the same place with the person I invited — please do

parts.note: to let something be is to leave it where it is
someone I invited is my guest

explanation.surface: A host urges a visitor to remain put with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite idiom granting permission, equivalent to go ahead.

clue.text: Playwright ignoring one rule with extremely tacky parody

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out

parts.note: Ben Travers was an English playwright of farces
R is the abbreviation for rule, and only one of the two in the name is dropped

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A dramatist breaks a convention with a tasteless send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of 1920s London; dropping an R from his name leaves TRAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation, a mocking parody.

clue.text: Attacker of Alsatians beaten up

indicators.note: beaten up means battered, so the dog breed's letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attacked a pair of guard dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is one who assaults, so a synonym for an attacker.

clue.text: As a result Whistler has nothing to enter at that point

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the official and nothing go into the place word

parts.note: there means at that point
a referee, REF, blows a whistle
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The painter Whistler has nothing to submit at that stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistler' suggests the American painter, but here it is the referee with a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A connective synonym: something following therefore follows as a consequence.

clue.text: Repaired end with Tom's daughter finding bits left over

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Tom's daughter fixed an end using scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are remnants, leftover scraps or odds and ends.

clue.text: The worst part? General Grievous's close

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fan asks whether the death of the Star Wars villain General Grievous was the worst bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment left at the bottom, the dregs, figuratively the worst part.

clue.text: Worth next to nothing a short time after? I hear likewise

indicators.note: after places the short time following the sound-alike
I hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: too means likewise, also
a bit is a short time, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: Something is worthless shortly afterwards, and someone claims to feel the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is American slang for cheap or trifling, worth next to nothing.

clue.text: Makes flat 50 finally available to golfer after the third of November

indicators.note: after puts the golfer behind the third letter

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter
the third of picks the third letter

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: Fifty is at last on offer to a golfer after early November.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: one who levels ground makes it flat.

clue.text: Whatever is not just wide of the mark

explanation.surface: Anything unfair also misses its target.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as a noun for an injustice and an adjective for being incorrect.

clue.text: Deck hands meeting over stopping work

indicators.note: stopping is plugging, so the letters go inside the work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
R and L are right and left, the two hands
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Crew members gather after downing tools on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, so a specific example.

clue.text: Special pleasure for puritan to seize loathsome drug

indicators.note: seizing holds inside, so the prude wraps the loathsome word

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous puritan
vile means loathsome
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A prude grabs a disgusting drug, a rare treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege can mean a special honour, as in it's a privilege to meet you.

clue.text: Previous priest admitting endless unrestrained revelry

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so the priest holds the revelry
endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a riot is unrestrained revelry

explanation.surface: A former cleric confesses to wild partying without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior engagement is a previous one, a synonym.

clue.text: Topic of interest for children

definitions.meaning: offspring, in the legal sense of died without heirs

explanation.surface: The question of kids comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a matter of debate and, formally, a person's offspring.

clue.text: Surprisingly liberal American taking in pole dancer

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so the pole goes inside
surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement of the letters

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A pole dancer is unexpectedly given a lift by a broad-minded American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' turns liberal into BALLERI; add A and the N goes inside before that last A.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a ballet dancer, an example of the category.

clue.text: Not entirely prepared to accept my grievance

indicators.note: accepting takes in, so the exclamation goes inside
not entirely means dropping the last letter

parts.note: set means ready, prepared
cor is an exclamation like my!

explanation.surface: Someone half-ready to accept a personal complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A score to settle is a grudge, a grievance.

clue.text: Starts to produce several texts during row with purveyor of inside info

indicators.note: during says the initials are placed within the row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats

indicators.note: starts to picks the initial letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone sends messages during an argument with a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster supplies betting or insider tips, so purveys inside information.

clue.text: She set out to take possession of The Head of Ulysses a mythical hero

indicators.note: taking possession holds something inside, so the rearranged letters wrap the initial
out implies the letters are worked out into a fresh arrangement
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman sets out to seize the bust of Ulysses, another mythical hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SHE SET into THESES, which holds U.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus slew the Minotaur in Greek myth, an example of a mythical hero.
